_comment: Paths are relative to SB/Content without extension. Field names follow USBShowRagdollKey (see assetkit/patch_shows.py ORDER). bIgnorePlayer defaults to true in the game's constructor, which is why vanilla Eve never ragdolls. Shared Dead_Monster_* shows stay vanilla; Eve gets her own clones (enemy impulses are 5k-18k and launch her). bOverrideHitBone=true makes the key push the bone that took the hit (the hit info's bone name, falling back to ImpulseBoneName when there is none); vanilla leaves it false, so every death pushed Spine1. Explosions keep the centre-of-mass push.

Art/Show/CH_P_EVE_01/Basic/P_Eve_Dead._comment: Animated deaths (with P_Eve_Dead2/3, _Nikke, Eve_Dead_Down): their ragdoll key is only the death signal. ImpulseLimitVelocity 701 marks it; main.lua sees the marker in RagdollInfo, turns physics back off and lets the show's own fall play (tune.active.animated). No knockdown show has a key, so a knockdown never counts
Art/Show/CH_P_EVE_01/Basic/P_Eve_Dead._comment_preload: The animated death's falls (EveDeath_*), each referenced by a play-show key of its own in the show's play-show channel, disabled and timed at 1e9 s, so they load and stay with her death show and are never played by it: UE4SS's LoadAsset didn't find them, a bare import was dropped by the IoStore conversion, and keys in no channel were garbage collected with the falls

Art/Show/CH_P_EVE_01/Basic/P_Eve_Dead_La._comment: Laser trap deaths (and P_EVE_Dead_Laser_BalanceBeam): vanilla plays a 2 s additive twitch with a shock decal and sparks and no ragdoll key, so she never simulated and main.lua never saw a death. The key starts her ragdoll 0.35 s into the jolt, a soft push (no blow to follow); the death then cuts like any other (a made-up blade, no skill hit)

Art/Show/CH_P_EVE_01/Ragdoll/EveDeath_Kn._comment_hold: hold: seconds the show runs on after the fall, on its last frame. It ended 0.9 s after, and the game's dead pose (her death show's, a different one) snapped in; 120 s outlasts the death screen (respawn reloads the level)
Art/Show/CH_P_EVE_01/Ragdoll/EveDeath_Kn._comment: Death animations made from her knockdown falls (the knockdown shows and animations stay as they are): P_Eve_Dead with the fall swapped in, held on its last frame, Eve_Dead_Common (the death face and voice) kept, no ragdoll key. main.lua plays one at random over an animated death (tune.active.animatedPool), F5 cycles through them

Art/Character/PC/CH_P_EVE_Head/CH_P_EVE_._comment: Eve's face (CH_P_EVE_01_Blueprint's face slot): LOD0 CPU access, so a beheading can move all of it onto the head bone (its neck is weighted to the neck, which stays)

Art/Character/PC/CH_P_EVE_01/Animation/F._comment: Eve's death face from Proper Death Expression by blabmice (third_party/proper-death-expression, credits there): the vanilla one is a blank stare

Art/Character/NPC/CH_NPC_AirborneSquad/C._comment: The Airborne Squad angels (tune.enemies.kinds N_AirborneSquad) wear CH_P_EVE_01_Body (the outfits job covers it) and CH_P_EVE_Face_003; their own body mesh (ST_AirborneSquad_MeshState may swap it in) and that face get LOD0 CPU access for their cuts

_comment_ui_delay: Seconds before the death/respawn UI appears, so the ragdoll is visible. Vanilla is 0 for these (desert hole uses 2.5).

Art/Character/PC/CH_P_EVE_01/Blueprints/._comment: Components attached to Eve's own skeleton that still block PhysicsBody. Once she ragdolls (Ragdoll profile = PhysicsBody) they push her own bodies every frame and fling her.

_comment_clone_retarget: Clones chain into the enemy Dead_Monster_Common (monster DEAD voice); Eve's own death shows chain into Eve_Dead_Common.

outfits._comment: Every outfit mesh EquipmentTable can put on Eve (SkeletalMesh on her body skeleton) gets LOD0 CPU access, which the gore slicer needs, and its physics asset gets the ragdoll fix. Vanilla physics assets enable Pelvis-vs-Thigh collision although the capsules overlap by ~10 cm at rest, which blows the ragdoll apart (the flinging), and disable almost everything else, so limbs pass through each other. Here bodies collide across groups and never inside one (some outfits, e.g. CH_P_EVE_09, ship with neighbouring torso bodies colliding, which spins her), except pairs closer than rest_margin cm in the outfit's bind pose (measured per asset by assetkit/outfits.py, for every body, so a jiggle, cape or accessory body resting inside another stops colliding with it). Linear damping 5.0 capped her fall at ~2 m/s (floaty); these bodies are kinematic in gameplay, so this only changes ragdolls. Hair and jiggle bodies keep their other settings. 'only' / 'skip' take mesh-name globs (e.g. only: ["CH_P_EVE_30*"]) to trim the mod; every patched mesh is a full copy in the pak and replaces outfit mods for the same mesh.
outfits._comment_cpuaccess: false: the outfit meshes are not repacked (only their physics assets): sbslice.dll keeps every skeletal mesh's LOD0 CPU copy at load (NeedCPUData), so the cut reads any outfit. The copies of outfit mods' meshes (SBPR's, 37 of them) crashed the game's async loader on some outfit changes (three crash dumps, all in the loader, right after CH_P_EVE_30). true repacks every mesh with LOD0 CPU access again, for a game without the DLL
outfits._comment_lock_orphans: Bodies no constraint holds (twist / helper bones anchoring a cape or skirt chain, e.g. CH_P_EVE_09's Ab-L-UpperArm-Tw1) fly free in a ragdoll and drag the skin off the limb; each gets a locked joint to the nearest ancestor body.
outfits._comment_accessory_collision: false: every body outside the groups (hair, cape, breast and hip jiggle, neck pieces) collides with nothing of hers, only the world. CH_P_EVE_09 had 114 such pairs with her main bodies; the jiggle bodies inside her torso shoved the thighs and arms and the cape got pinned under her, and she shook on the floor
outfits._comment_self_collision: false: none of her bodies collide with each other at all, only with the world. With the groups colliding, an arm or leg landing on her own body set every joint jittering until each part found the floor (eighteenth playtest), and the runtime switch (tune.selfCollision, the mesh ignoring PhysicsBody) didn't stop it. Limbs may pass through her now
outfits._comment_lock_below: With hard_limits, a main joint's motion limited to fewer degrees than this is locked instead. Hard limits a few degrees wide (clavicles 5, the shoulder's roll 5, the hip's sideways swing 5, the neck 5, pelvis to spine twist 5) sat at their limit all the time and every joint buzzed, even in mid-air (eighteenth playtest)
outfits._comment_locked_joints: Joints locked whole (none now). Locking the clavicles (they buzzed in their 15 deg twist) hung both arms rigidly off the light neck, and the spine and pelvis buzzed on 40-60% of ticks instead (eighteenth playtest)
outfits._comment_body: Damping on the torso and limb bodies: vanilla linear 5.0 capped her fall at ~2 m/s, angular 10.0 made her topple and turn as if under water (both only matter in a ragdoll, the bodies are kinematic in gameplay)
outfits._comment_limits: The main joints bend about their twist axis (PhAT framed them as hinges), limited the same both ways round a zero of the asset's own, as soft limits: vanilla knees went 19 deg past straight, elbows 24, hips bent forward only 30 and back as far, the spine 5 deg a joint, and the soft limits gave way further under a push (she folded at odd angles). 'ranges': how far each joint's far end ('end') may swing towards her front and her back from the bind pose, in degrees; outfits.py measures each asset's zero and turns its frame 2 to centre the range ('limits' in the expanded spec). 'swing' overrides cone limits (Swing1 = sideways for the hips). 'hard_limits': every angular limit of the grouped bodies' joints stops dead instead of springing (bSoftConstraint off).
